text:
sam: heads-up — apiserver 502/503 spikes in us-west1 since 08:12 UTC. started around the same time as a GPU-attach surge from a big batch rollout. seeing high WAL fsync latencies on etcd leader around the same window.
infra-bot: ALERT: [us-west1] apiserver error rate > 5% for 3m (P99 latency 420ms) — Pager sent to #eng-sre oncall.
oncall-sre: investigating, grabbing logs and charts. which clusters are affected?
sam: cluster: prod-usw1-gpu. Attach controller churn increases pod creation rate -> many ephemeral NAT connections. conntrack and NAT metrics both spike.
viv: got kube-proxy conntrack counts:
```
conntrack: entries 638976 (est), max 655360
snat_used: 12123, snat_available: 377
```
viv: SNAT pools look nearly exhausted; NAT gateway CPU also spiking. also seeing a flood of SYN_RECV on the NAT side.
jess: etctd logs show repeated slow fsyncs and WAL flush stalls:
```
I180320 08:12:45 etcdserver: 0.0.0.0:56789 accepted connection
W180320 08:12:46 wal: sync took 245ms
E180320 08:12:47 raft: election timeout elapsed, starting election
```
jess: leader had increased IO wait; pod eviction/leader flips around the same minutes.
michael: apiserver traces show high backend errors when controller-manager hits etcd leader flip. controller-manager restarted once due to leader-elected lock contention.
oncall-sre: sounds like SNAT exhaustion -> connections failing -> apiserver proxy/TCP resets -> clients retry -> more attach churn -> more load on etcd. vicious loop.
sam: exact. attach controller is pretty aggressive on that rollout (parallel attaches 300+). We pushed a canary with many small pods.
viv: quick mitigation idea: throttle attach controller concurrency via feature-flagged config or apply a k8s patch to reduce threadpool on the provisioner. Also scale NAT gateway horizontally and increase SNAT ports.
jess: agree. immediate steps: 1) scale NAT gateway + add second NAT to spread source IPs 2) bump conntrack max on nodes + kube-proxy tune 3) temporarily reduce attach-controller concurrency in rollout OR pause rollout.
michael: we should also enable short-term apiserver circuit-breaker: set max-inflight-requests and reduce long-running request timeouts to protect controlplane.
sam: doing step 3 now — paused the rollout. notifying infra about NAT scaling.
viv: running rollout pause: `kubectl -n infra rollout pause deployment/gpu-batch` — done. CPU and NAT metrics already trending down.
infra-bot: Infrastructure request created: NAT-scaling-ticket #INC-4921 (priority P1) — assigned to cloud-networking.
oncall-sre: for postmortem: need to consider backpressure in provisioning pipeline so spikes don't collapse controlplane. Also evaluate using managed private IPs for attaches to avoid SNAT dependence.
jess: note on etctd side: WAL fsyncs increase when disk queue waits and when leader flips. once NAT is scaled and attach throttled, we should watch WAL latency for 30m before marking healthy.
viv: heatmap shows p99 etcd fsync decreased to 45ms after pause + NAT scale started.
michael: action items captured: [sam] pause rollout (done), [viv] coord NAT scale + conntrack bump, [jess] watch etcd WAL + collect logs, [oncall-sre] run RCA and schedule follow-up.
oncall-sre: quick ask — can we add a short-term rate limiter at the attach-controller side to cap new attach requests from the orchestrator? that'd prevent spikes in future.
sam: filing a small change now, will feature-flag it.
jess: moving to monitoring tasks: add dashboards for SNAT usage, conntrack headroom, etcd fsync p99, and apiserver backend error rates per region.
viv: also tagging cost note: scaling NAT gateways has cost impact; long-term solution is to reduce SNAT dependency or use more ephemeral private IPs for bursts. include cost estimate in the RCA.
oncall-sre: good. closing alert in 10m if rates stay <1% and etcd fsync p99 < 100ms.
infra-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: [us-west1] apiserver error rate returned to baseline (0.8%).
